claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is a single-phase high-entropy alloy that can be studied from an initially coarse-grained state.
The relevant initial state lacks significant grain-boundary segregation and intermetallic precipitation.
Severe sliding deformation can transform an initially coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi surface into an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The same dynamic refinement occurs generally under high-strain-rate deformation outside sliding contact.
The dynamically refined layer can develop cavitation-induced nanoporosity without significant segregation or phase separation.
A high average high-angle grain-boundary energy implies a propensity for localized cohesive failure at grain boundaries.
Cavitation preferentially initiates at high-angle grain boundaries and triple junctions.
The dynamically refined grains are 10–50 nm in size.
Below a critical grain size, dislocation-mediated plasticity is suppressed in favor of grain-boundary sliding.
Grain-boundary sliding reduces grain-boundary cohesion and thereby causes nanocavitation.
Refinement-induced nanocavitation causes premature brittle failure and degradation of fracture toughness.
The proposed mechanism is distinct from embrittlement caused by impurity segregation or intermetallic precipitation.
Samples that form an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer will have lower toughness and more brittle, intergranular fracture than the coarse-grained baseline.
Formation of the refined layer will increase wear-particle generation through cavitation events.
Pre-annealing will create a coarse surface microstructure that resists subsequent dynamic refinement.
A pre-annealed coarse-grained comparison sample will retain higher toughness and show less nanoporosity-induced decohesion.
Inverse Hall–Petch behavior, low friction, and an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer coexist during UHV sliding of CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed degradation mechanism is limited principally to high-rate or low-friction sliding conditions in chemically inert environments.
At low strain rates, dynamic refinement and its proposed embrittlement mechanism are absent.
Dynamic amorphization is expected to be activated from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
